sections.heading: How Action Recommendations Work in AI Visibility Platforms
paragraphs: Monitoring brand mentions tells you where you stand, but it leaves a manual analysis problem: reading hundreds of AI responses and cited URLs to figure out what to do next. Action recommendation engines automate that triage. They compare the prompts where your brand is absent or negatively framed against the sources answer engines actually cite, then output a prioritized queue of work.

Because [84% of cited links point to domains the brand does not own](/blog/where-ai-citations-come-from), useful recommendations have to look beyond your own blog. In Elmo, the [Opportunities engine](/features/aeo-recommendations) turns tracked visibility and [citation analysis](/features/citation-tracking) into a regularly refreshed list of what to create on your site, which third-party publishers to pitch, and which community threads to seed. Tools that also capture [query fan-out](/ai-visibility-tools/features/query-fan-out)—the background web searches an assistant runs before answering—can show the exact sub-queries your pages miss.

sections.heading: What Separates Useful AEO Action Plans From Generic Advice
paragraphs: Not every recommendation engine is worth acting on. Some platforms pass your prompt list to an LLM and return generic SEO advice, or score pages against static checklists that have little bearing on whether an answer engine will cite you. Before buying a tool for its action items, check how those recommendations are derived and whether you can verify the impact.

items.title: Grounded in Cited Sources, Not Static Scores
items.body: [Engine-free content scores do not reliably predict AI citations](/blog/can-content-scores-predict-ai-citations). Look for recommendations tied directly to the URLs and passages answer engines cite for your tracked prompts, not generic readability grades.

items.title: Alert-Driven and Scheduled Prioritization

Out of the 96 tools on this page, 29 pair action recommendations with [email alerts](/ai-visibility-tools/features/email-alerts) (including Profound, Peec AI, Trakkr, and Wellows), while tools like ChatRank and AmIOnAI organize work into weekly task inboxes.

Tools like Elmo keep the raw engine output and passages inspectable, and platforms like Prominara and Siftly re-run prompts against baselines or control groups to see what actually moved.

sections.heading: How AI Crawler Analytics Works and Where It Falls Short
paragraphs: When an AI search engine grounds an answer or refreshes its index, automated user agents fetch your pages. AI crawler analytics records those visits so you can see which bots access your site, which URLs they request most often, and where they encounter errors or blocks. In tools like Indexly, Canonry, and Cairrot, this data comes from ingesting server logs (such as Vercel or Cloud Run logs) or installing a CMS plugin on WordPress, while platforms like Topify include an AI Robots Checker to verify your access rules.

Crawler data is a diagnostic input, not a visibility metric on its own. A bot visit confirms that an agent fetched your HTML, but it does not guarantee that the engine parsed your content or cited your domain in an answer. As our research on [whether AI crawlers render JavaScript](/blog/do-ai-crawlers-render-javascript) shows, most AI crawlers fetch raw HTML and skip client-side rendering, meaning a status-200 log entry can still leave an agent with an empty page.

Blocking or misconfiguring bots is another common failure mode. Leftover rules in your [robots.txt for AI crawlers](/blog/robots-txt-ai-crawlers) can silently block search grounding bots while you are trying to block training scrapers. Crawler analytics helps you confirm that [AI agents can read your website](/blog/can-ai-agents-read-your-website), while downstream [citation analytics](/ai-visibility-tools/features/citation-analytics) proves whether those crawls actually turn into cited answers.

sections.heading: How AI Keyword Research Differs From Traditional SEO Keyword Tools
paragraphs: Traditional SEO keyword research relies on short head terms and search engine autocomplete data. In contrast, [answer engine optimization](/blog/aeo-vs-seo) requires understanding full conversational prompts, persona-specific constraints, and follow-up questions. Because AI platforms do not publish a public equivalent of Google Keyword Planner, AI visibility platforms have to assemble prompt discovery from several different signals.

Some platforms generate candidate prompts by analyzing your domain, product pages, and entities to simulate buyer questions. Others adapt traditional search data: LLMClicks.ai uses Google Search Console data to identify queries that trigger brand mentions, while tools like Semrush AI Toolkit and Ahrefs Brand Radar connect AI tracking to their existing keyword databases. A third group mines captured conversation datasets: Writesonic draws on a dataset of over 2 billion AI conversations, and Aiso collects real multi-turn sessions on the premise that a median of 59% of what users say happens after the opening question.

Another major signal is [query fan-out](/features/query-fan-out). When an answer engine grounds a response using web search, it often rewrites the user's conversational prompt into several shorter search queries. Tools like Elmo, Rankscale, Finseo, and ALLMO record these underlying searches, showing you the exact wording models use to retrieve sources and which sub-queries your existing pages win or miss.

sections.heading: How Brand Mention Tracking Works in AI Search
paragraphs: Unlike web or social media listening, where a crawler can index a public feed of posts, AI conversations are private and generated on the fly. To monitor brand mentions in AI search, [AI visibility tracking](/features/ai-visibility-tracking) tools run a set of representative buyer prompts against target engines on a recurring schedule and parse the resulting responses for your brand name, product names, aliases, and domains.

This distinction matters because a brand mention is not the same thing as a link. Research on [ghost citations](/blog/ghost-citations) shows that AI engines frequently cite a company's URL as a grounding source without naming the brand in the answer text—and conversely, models often recommend well-known brands from training weights without citing their websites at all. Proper monitoring tracks [brand mentions](/glossary/brand-mention) and [citation analytics](/ai-visibility-tools/features/citation-analytics) as separate metrics.

Because generative answers vary from run to run, a single check rarely tells the truth. Reliable trackers run prompts repeatedly across multiple engines, normalize the text, and aggregate the results into an overall visibility rate and [AI share of voice](/blog/ai-share-of-voice) against your competitors.

sections.heading: What Separates Accurate Brand Monitoring From Noise

items.title: Entity Disambiguation and Aliases
items.body: If your brand shares a name with a common noun, a city, or another company, basic keyword matching will inflate your numbers. Look for tools that configure brand aliases, match associated domains, and use an LLM or entity parser to verify that a mention actually refers to your company.

items.title: Real Consumer UI vs. Model APIs

Tools that capture [real UI answers](/ai-visibility-tools/features/real-ui-answers) via scraping providers reflect the actual grounding, system prompts, and shopping carousels that real users encounter.

items.title: Position and Recommendation Context
items.body: Being named first in a shortlist of three vendors is very different from being mentioned last with a caveat. Strong platforms pair mention detection with [sentiment analysis](/ai-visibility-tools/features/sentiment-analysis) and average position tracking, and let you inspect the exact passage that triggered the score.

items.title: Hallucination and Fact Checking
items.body: Counting mentions is only half the job when an engine is repeating outdated pricing or confusing your product with a competitor's. Tools like Waikay, BrandRank.AI, and SiteSignal explicitly monitor for inaccurate claims and narrative drift alongside mention frequency.

sections.heading: How Bring Your Own Keys Works in AI Visibility Tracking
paragraphs: Most AI visibility platforms bundle prompt execution into rigid subscription tiers, charging a steep markup on every run. When a tool supports Bring Your Own Keys (BYOK), it separates the software interface and analytics layer from the underlying data collection and inference costs. You paste your own API credentials into the platform and pay the upstream providers directly on your own invoice.

In practice, BYOK covers two distinct categories of credentials. First are direct model APIs—such as OpenAI, Anthropic, Mistral, Gemini, and OpenRouter—which are used either to query models directly or to parse responses for brand mentions and [sentiment analysis](/features/sentiment-analysis). Second are scraping provider keys—such as Cloro, BrightData, Oxylabs, SearchApi, Olostep, and DataForSEO—which capture [real UI answers](/ai-visibility-tools/features/real-ui-answers) from consumer surfaces like ChatGPT, Google AI Overviews, Google AI Mode, and Perplexity.

Elmo is built natively around this model. When you self-host the open-source MIT codebase for free, you configure your own scraping and model keys in the [providers setup](/docs/user-guide/providers) and pay zero software fees. If you prefer not to manage infrastructure, Elmo Cloud starts at $29/mo while keeping the same transparent architecture.

A reliable BYOK implementation needs background workers, queue management, and provider fallbacks rather than firing requests from a browser tab.

sections.heading: How AI Citation Tracking Works and Where It Hits Limits
paragraphs: When an answer engine responds to a prompt using web search, it retrieves candidate pages and attaches source links to its answer. Tools with [citation tracking](/features/citation-tracking) capture those responses on a schedule, extract every cited URL and its position, and aggregate the links by page, domain, and source category. In Elmo, for example, every cited URL is stored in PostgreSQL and categorized into your own domains, competitor domains, social media, Google properties, and institutional sources.

Measuring [AI citations](/blog/ai-citations) is the most direct way to see which third-party publishers and owned pages shape an engine's answers in your category. Because [84% of cited links point to domains the brand does not own](/blog/where-ai-citations-come-from), domain-level and URL-level rollups reveal whether your visibility problem is an on-site content gap or an off-site earned media gap. Pairing citation counts with [brand mention tracking](/ai-visibility-tools/features/brand-mention-tracking) also exposes [ghost citations](/blog/ghost-citations), where an engine cites your URL as a source without naming your brand in the prose.

Practitioners should account for three structural limits when reading citation reports. First, [citation volatility](/blog/citation-volatility) is high across runs, and [different AI engines rarely cite the same sources](/blog/do-ai-engines-cite-the-same-sources) even when their prose answers agree. Second, raw model APIs and consumer web interfaces return different citation sets; for example, [ChatGPT UI and API citation behavior](/blog/chatgpt-ui-reddit-citations-api) has diverged historically before converging on specific domains. Third, an attached link does not guarantee endorsement or accuracy—audits show [roughly a third of AI citations do not support the claim](/blog/can-you-trust-ai-citations) they are attached to.

sections.heading: How Competitor Benchmarking Works in AI Search

sections.heading: How Content Gap Analysis Works in AI Search
paragraphs: In traditional SEO, a content gap is a keyword your competitors rank for in Google's top ten while your domain does not. In [answer engine optimization](/blog/aeo-vs-seo), the mechanics are different. When an AI assistant answers a buyer's question, it synthesizes a response from training data and live web retrieval, mentioning a handful of brands and citing specific URLs as evidence. An AI content gap occurs when competitors are named or cited in those answers and your brand is absent.

Because [most cited URLs point to third-party domains](/blog/where-ai-citations-come-from) rather than a brand's own website, AEO gap analysis has to look beyond your blog. A complete analysis separates gaps into three distinct buckets: missing owned pages on your site, missing third-party citations on publisher or community sites where rivals are featured, and missing sub-queries during [query fan-out](/features/query-fan-out)—the background web searches an engine runs to ground its answer.

Elmo handles this by combining [competitor benchmarking](/ai-visibility-tools/features/competitor-benchmarking), [citation analytics](/features/citation-tracking), and query fan-out recording into a prioritized Opportunities list. For every tracked prompt, Elmo logs which web searches the engine ran, categorizes every cited URL (competitor domains, social media, institutional sources), and highlights where your content misses the grounding searches or where third-party outlets cite rivals instead of you.

sections.heading: What Separates Strong Gap Analysis From Basic Mention Diffs
paragraphs: Many tools check the box for content gap analysis simply by filtering a table to show prompts where your brand mention count is zero and a competitor's is greater than one. While knowing where you are invisible is a starting point, a prompt list alone does not tell a writer what to build or a PR team who to pitch. When evaluating the 74 tools in this directory, check how deeply they diagnose the reason behind the gap.

items.title: Owned vs. Earned Source Separation
items.body: If a competitor wins a prompt because ChatGPT cites their comparison guide, you have a content creation gap. If they win because Perplexity cites a G2 crowd list, a Reddit thread, or a trade publication, writing a blog post on your own domain will rarely fix it. Tools like Xofu, Prominara, and Elmo separate owned-page gaps from third-party publisher and community targets.

items.title: Query Fan-Out Visibility
items.body: Assistants rarely search the exact 20-word prompt a user types; they rewrite it into shorter web searches. Platforms that capture [query fan-out](/ai-visibility-tools/features/query-fan-out)—such as Elmo, Peec AI, LLMrefs, and Finseo—show the exact background searches your pages failed to match, giving your SEO team concrete phrases to target.

items.title: Fact and Entity Coverage vs. Prompt Presence
items.body: Sometimes an engine omits your brand not because you lack a landing page, but because it cannot verify a specific capability, pricing tier, or integration. Entity-focused tools like Waikay and BrandRank.AI inspect whether models hold outdated claims or missing facts about your product compared to category leaders.

items.title: Multi-Engine Disagreement
items.body: Academic audits show that [different AI engines cite vastly different sources](/blog/do-ai-engines-cite-the-same-sources) even when answering the same question. A gap analysis tied to a single model API will misdirect your content roadmap. Look for [multi-engine tracking](/features/multi-engine-tracking) that captures real consumer UIs across ChatGPT, Google AI Overviews, Google AI Mode, and Perplexity.

sections.heading: How Email Alerts Work in AI Visibility Tracking (and Why They Can Be Noisy)
paragraphs: Email alerts in AI visibility tools fall into two categories: scheduled summary digests (daily or weekly rollups of your [visibility score](/glossary/visibility-score), share of voice, and citation counts) and threshold-triggered notifications that fire when a metric crosses a line. Teams use them to catch sudden drops in brand mentions, spot a competitor taking over a high-intent buying prompt, or flag negative [AI brand sentiment](/blog/ai-brand-sentiment) without logging into a dashboard every morning.

The catch is that generative answers are non-deterministic. Ask ChatGPT or Perplexity the same question twice in an hour and the wording, brand order, and cited URLs often shift on their own. Because of this natural [citation volatility](/blog/citation-volatility), a tool that fires an email every time a single prompt run changes will quickly flood your inbox with false alarms.

How often a tool samples each prompt determines whether an alert represents a real shift or random variance. Before relying on automated emails to brief executives or trigger content rewrites, check how the platform aggregates runs and how [prompt tracking cadence](/blog/ai-prompt-tracking) affects the numbers behind the notification.

sections.heading: How Tracking Brand Visibility in Gemini Actually Works
paragraphs: When marketers talk about Google's AI answers, three separate surfaces often get conflated: the standalone [Gemini](/ai-search/gemini) app, [Google AI Overviews](/ai-visibility-tools/features/google-ai-overviews) at the top of traditional search results, and [Google AI Mode](/ai-visibility-tools/features/google-ai-mode). Although they share underlying model families, they run different retrieval pipelines, trigger web search on different thresholds, and cite different domains. Tracking one does not tell you how your brand appears in the others—research on [whether AI engines cite the same sources](/blog/do-ai-engines-cite-the-same-sources) shows that even Google's own AI surfaces have minimal citation overlap.

To track visibility in Gemini, software runs a defined set of buyer prompts on a recurring schedule, parses the responses for your brand name, aliases, and domains, and records every cited URL. Tools collect these answers in one of two ways: by calling Google's Gemini API directly, or by scraping the live consumer web interface via providers like Cloro, BrightData, Oxylabs, SearchApi, Olostep, or DataForSEO. Because the consumer app applies its own system prompts, conversation formatting, and Google Search grounding behavior, tools that capture [real UI answers](/ai-visibility-tools/features/real-ui-answers) reflect what buyers actually read far better than bare API calls.

Whenever Gemini grounds an answer in live web search, it rewrites the user's prompt into one or more background search queries before synthesizing a reply. Tools that support [query fan-out analysis](/features/query-fan-out) capture those underlying searches, showing which terms Gemini adds or drops and which specific web searches your pages win or miss.

items.title: Query Fan-Out Inspection

sections.heading: How Google AI Mode Tracking Works and Why Search Console Is Not Enough
paragraphs: [Google AI Mode](/glossary/google-ai-mode) is Google's dedicated conversational search interface, separate from the [Google AI Overviews](/ai-visibility-tools/features/google-ai-overviews) summary box that appears above traditional organic results. While [Google Search Console now includes generative AI impressions](/blog/search-console-ai-visibility), it blends AI Mode and AI Overviews into aggregate metrics and omits the exact conversational prompts, cited URLs, and competitor mentions. To see what buyers actually read when they evaluate your category in AI Mode, teams have to run scheduled prompt tracking against the live interface.

Because Google does not offer a public API that reproduces the consumer AI Mode experience, trackers must capture answers from the real web interface using specialized [LLM scraping APIs](/blog/best-llm-scraping-apis) such as Cloro, BrightData, Oxylabs, SearchApi, Olostep, or DataForSEO. When a prompt runs, AI Mode breaks the question into multiple background web searches—a process known as [query fan-out](/features/query-fan-out)—before synthesizing a response and attaching source links. A complete tracker captures the rendered answer text, the exact URLs and domains cited, and those underlying fan-out searches.

Keeping AI Mode and AI Overviews separate in your reporting is essential. Research shows that [even Google's own two AI surfaces disagree on cited sources](/blog/do-ai-engines-cite-the-same-sources), meaning a page that wins a citation in a standard SERP overview may be completely absent when a user switches to conversational AI Mode. Tools like Elmo track both surfaces independently from the real consumer UI, storing the raw output in PostgreSQL so every mention, [sentiment score](/features/sentiment-analysis), and citation trend can be audited.

sections.heading: How Google AI Overviews Tracking Works and Where It Hits Limits
paragraphs: Unlike standalone chat apps where every prompt produces a reply, [Google AI Overviews](/ai-search/google-ai-overviews) only trigger on a subset of Google searches. Even though [AI Overviews appear in over 40% of US searches](/blog/ai-overviews-share-of-searches) and increasingly show up on [branded searches](/blog/ai-overviews-for-brand-searches), a tracker first has to record whether an overview rendered at all for a given query before checking for your brand.

Because Google does not offer a public API that returns AI Overview text and citations, tools must capture the live search results page. Platforms like Elmo use scraping providers (such as Cloro, BrightData, Oxylabs, SearchApi, Olostep, and DataForSEO) to fetch the real consumer surface, then parse the overview body for brand mentions, sentiment, competitor rank, and cited URLs. You can also check Google's native reporting, though [Google Search Console's generative AI report](/blog/search-console-ai-visibility) blends AI Overviews and AI Mode impressions together and omits query-level citation data.

The main operational limit is volatility and surface divergence. Google runs two distinct generative experiences in search, and research shows that [AI engines rarely cite the same sources](/blog/do-ai-engines-cite-the-same-sources) — even between Google's own AI Overviews and AI Mode. Furthermore, [ranking in Google's top 10](/blog/rankings-and-ai-citations) is neither necessary nor sufficient for earning an AI Overview citation, so traditional rank trackers cannot substitute for dedicated overview parsing.

sections.heading: How MCP Servers Work in AI Visibility Platforms
paragraphs: The Model Context Protocol (MCP) is a standard that connects AI assistants and coding environments to external data sources and tools. When an AI visibility platform ships an MCP server, you can connect clients like Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, or VS Code directly to your tracking account without exporting CSVs or writing custom [REST API](/ai-visibility-tools/features/data-export-api) scripts.

Instead of clicking through a web dashboard to check why your visibility dropped, you can ask your assistant to pull recent answers, compare [competitor share of voice](/features/share-of-voice), or list the domains cited on a specific prompt tag. Depending on the platform, the MCP server may be read-only (fetching visibility scores, sentiment, and citations) or support write actions like adding prompts, triggering runs, and updating brand configurations.

In [Elmo's API and MCP](/features/api-and-mcp) implementation, for example, Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, and VS Code can both query tracked analytics and manage prompts. However, an MCP server is only as useful as the underlying dataset: if a tracker only queries raw model APIs without web search or lacks [citation analytics](/ai-visibility-tools/features/citation-analytics), querying it from Cursor will still return incomplete answers.

For example, Notra queries ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Perplexity, and Google AI Overviews with web search enabled, but queries Meta's models, Grok, and DeepSeek without web search. Conversely, tools like Rankshift and Rankscale explicitly distinguish between chat-interface results and raw model responses so you know whether you are measuring pre-trained brand recall or live retrieval.

In Elmo, [multi-engine tracking](/features/multi-engine-tracking) connects to OpenRouter and direct model APIs using your own provider keys alongside consumer surface scrapers, storing the raw output and model version in PostgreSQL so every mention and citation is auditable. Because [AI engines rarely cite the same sources](/blog/do-ai-engines-cite-the-same-sources), separating ungrounded Llama model priors from grounded web answers is essential before you change your content strategy.

sections.heading: How Microsoft Copilot Visibility Tracking Works
paragraphs: Unlike traditional rank trackers that check static SERP positions, a Copilot SEO tracker runs buyer prompts on a schedule and parses the generated answers. For each run, the software records whether your brand was named, where it appeared relative to competitors, the sentiment of the passage, and which URLs Copilot cited to ground its response. Because AI answers vary from run to run, reliable tools aggregate multiple runs over time into a [visibility score](/glossary/visibility-score) and [share of voice](/features/share-of-voice) trend rather than relying on a single snapshot.

How a tool collects Copilot responses matters as much as what it measures. Microsoft does not offer a public API that reproduces the exact consumer Copilot experience, so platforms either approximate answers via raw model APIs or capture the actual web interface using scraping providers. In Elmo, background workers capture the real Microsoft Copilot consumer surface via providers like Cloro, BrightData, Oxylabs, SearchApi, Olostep, and DataForSEO, storing the raw output, cited URLs, and [query fan-out](/features/query-fan-out) searches in PostgreSQL so every metric can be audited.

Teams tracking Copilot can also pair third-party prompt trackers with Microsoft's own first-party tooling. As we cover in our guide to [Microsoft Clarity AI citations](/blog/microsoft-clarity-ai-citations), Clarity offers a free dashboard showing which of your pages are cited inside the Microsoft ecosystem, though it cannot show your share of voice on prompts where competitors win the citation instead of you.

sections.heading: Why AI Answers Change Rapidly Across Languages
paragraphs: Running a translated prompt in ChatGPT, Perplexity, or Google AI Overviews does not simply translate the English answer. When an answer engine grounds a response in German, French, Japanese, or Spanish, its [query fan-out](/ai-visibility-tools/features/query-fan-out) usually runs web searches in that target language. That pulls in an entirely different pool of regional publishers, local review sites, and country-specific directories.

Even when two engines answer the same question in the same market, [they rarely cite the same domains](/blog/do-ai-engines-cite-the-same-sources). Across languages, the divergence is even wider: a software brand that dominates English citations on Reddit and G2 may be invisible in French or German answers if local media and regional comparison portals only cover domestic competitors.

Model training weights also vary by language. Western models like Claude and ChatGPT have different pre-training corpora than models with heavy non-English adoption like [DeepSeek](/ai-visibility-tools/features/deepseek) or Mistral. Tracking prompts in the exact phrasing your local buyers use is the only reliable way to measure international [AI share of voice](/blog/ai-share-of-voice).

sections.heading: Why Single-Engine Tracking Misses the Picture
paragraphs: Relying on a single AI assistant to judge your brand visibility fails because [AI engines rarely cite the same sources](/blog/do-ai-engines-cite-the-same-sources). Even within the same company, Google's two generative surfaces—[Google AI Overviews](/ai-visibility-tools/features/google-ai-overviews) and [Google AI Mode](/ai-visibility-tools/features/google-ai-mode)—disagree on citations and brand mentions.

Source preferences also swing wildly between platforms. For example, [YouTube is the top-cited domain in Google's AI answers](/blog/youtube-ai-citations) while barely registering in ChatGPT, and publishers with OpenAI licensing deals earn a citation premium in ChatGPT that does not carry over to Perplexity or Google. Multi-LLM trackers run the exact same prompt schedule across every major engine so you can separate an isolated model quirk from a category-wide visibility gap.

A reliable [multi-engine tracking](/features/multi-engine-tracking) pipeline normalizes brand aliases, domains, sentiment, and citation positions the same way on every run so scores can be compared side by side.

sections.heading: How Perplexity Rank Tracking Works (And Why It Differs From SEO)
paragraphs: Unlike traditional search engines that return a static page of ten blue links for a keyword, [Perplexity](/ai-search/perplexity) is an answer engine that synthesizes responses in real time. When a user submits a prompt, Perplexity often rewrites the question into multiple background web searches—a process known as [query fan-out](/features/query-fan-out)—retrieves the top pages, and generates a cited summary. Because there is no fixed SERP position, Perplexity rank tracking measures two distinct things: whether your brand is named in the generated text (and in what order among competitors), and whether your domain is linked in the numbered source footnotes.

How a tracker collects those answers determines what you actually measure. Some tools query model APIs, while others capture the consumer web interface via [real UI answers](/ai-visibility-tools/features/real-ui-answers). As tools like Qwairy and Rankscale explicitly highlight in their methodologies, API responses and what users see in the consumer UI frequently diverge. Elmo captures Perplexity from the real consumer app through scraping providers while storing the cited URLs, the underlying web searches, and the exact passage where your brand or a competitor was mentioned.

Even when Perplexity cites a URL, the citation alone does not guarantee your brand was recommended—or that the source says what the model claims. Over 60% of brand appearances in AI answers are [ghost citations](/blog/ghost-citations) where a domain is linked in the footnotes without the company being named in the text, and independent audits show [roughly a third of Perplexity's citations](/blog/can-you-trust-ai-citations) do not substantiate the sentence they are attached to. A capable Perplexity tracker separates footnote link counts from actual in-text brand mentions and sentiment.

sections.heading: How Prompt Volume Estimates Work (and Why None Are Exact)
paragraphs: Practitioners frequently ask which tool provides real [prompt volume](/glossary/prompt-volume) data rather than estimates. The honest answer is none of them. Because first-party engine logs are closed, every vendor on this page models demand using proxy signals. Unlike short keywords, conversational prompts are phrased differently by almost every user, and [multi-turn conversations](/blog/multi-turn-ai-search) hide much of the intent in follow-up messages. A useful prompt volume metric clusters semantically similar questions into an intent topic rather than pretending thousands of people type the exact same twelve-word sentence.

sections.heading: How Query Fan-Out Works in AI Search
paragraphs: When a user asks an answer engine a complex question, the model rarely searches the web using that exact sentence. During [grounding](/glossary/grounding), engines like ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Google AI Mode break the prompt down and run several shorter, targeted web searches in the background. A single buyer question might fan out into three or four distinct search queries covering product comparisons, pricing, and recent reviews before the engine synthesizes its final response.

In the AI visibility software market, vendors use the term query fan-out in two distinct ways. First, in platforms like Elmo and ALLMO, [query fan-out analysis](/features/query-fan-out) means recording the actual background web searches an answer engine executes during retrieval-augmented generation, showing which words the engine adds, drops, or keeps from your tracked prompt. Second, tools like LLMrefs use fan-out to describe an automated query fan-out generator that expands a seed SEO keyword into a cluster of conversational prompts to track.

Both mechanisms solve a core blind spot in [answer engine optimization](/glossary/answer-engine-optimization). If you only look at the prompt you typed and the final answer, you cannot see why a competitor was cited instead of you. Inspecting the fan-out searches reveals the exact retrieval queries your pages need to win to enter the model's context window.

sections.heading: Why Real Consumer UI Answers Diverge From Model APIs
paragraphs: When a buyer asks a question in the ChatGPT web app, Perplexity, or Google Search, the answer they read is not the raw output of an LLM API call. Consumer AI applications wrap the base model in custom system prompts, proprietary web-search retrieval pipelines, safety and brand filters, and UI-specific formatting such as citation carousels, shopping cards, and inline source links. Calling a developer endpoint like the OpenAI or Anthropic API bypasses much of that product layer, even when web search parameters are enabled.

Because of this architectural gap, API-only trackers often report different brand mentions and [AI citations](/blog/ai-citations) than a human user sees on screen. While some gaps have narrowed—for example, [ChatGPT UI Reddit citation rates](/blog/chatgpt-ui-reddit-citations-api) eventually converged toward the levels returned by the OpenAI web search API—significant differences remain across engines in how queries are rewritten and which domains get cited. Google's consumer surfaces ([Google AI Overviews](/ai-visibility-tools/features/google-ai-overviews) and [Google AI Mode](/ai-visibility-tools/features/google-ai-mode)) do not even have direct model API equivalents, meaning they can only be measured by capturing the live search interface.

Capturing the real UI requires browser automation and residential proxy networks to render the consumer apps, extract the full response markdown, and parse the exact cited URLs and [query fan-out](/features/query-fan-out) searches. It is slower and more expensive to run than firing off API requests, which is why most tools in our directory still default to APIs. For teams that need to audit how their data is collected, Elmo captures consumer surfaces (ChatGPT, Google AI Overviews, Google AI Mode, Gemini, Perplexity, and Microsoft Copilot) via [LLM scraping APIs](/blog/best-llm-scraping-apis) like Cloro, BrightData, Oxylabs, SearchApi, Olostep, and DataForSEO, while allowing users to bring their own provider keys.

sections.heading: How Sentiment Analysis Works in AI Visibility Software
paragraphs: [Brand mention tracking](/ai-visibility-tools/features/brand-mention-tracking) tells you how often an answer engine names your company, but a high mention rate can hide a reputation problem if the assistant warns buyers about your pricing, cites a three-year-old outage, or recommends a competitor instead. [AI brand sentiment analysis](/blog/ai-brand-sentiment) reads the surrounding context of every mention to measure how models actually characterize your product.

In practice, an AI visibility tool runs a set of prompts on a schedule, parses the responses for your brand and competitor names, and uses a language model or natural language classifier to evaluate the tone toward each company named. In [Elmo's sentiment analysis](/features/sentiment-analysis), every answer that names your brand or a rival is classified as positive (100), neutral or mixed (50), or negative (0). Those judgments roll up into a 0–100 score per prompt, per model, and against each competitor, while storing the exact passage that triggered the score so you can inspect the raw response in PostgreSQL.

Sentiment in AI answers has limits you should account for when reading a dashboard. Models frequently hedge with pros-and-cons lists on comparison queries, which produces a high share of neutral or mixed scores even for category leaders. And because AI search engines [rarely verify suspicious claims](/blog/ai-search-fact-checking), a single negative Reddit thread or outdated review article in the model's retrieval set can swing sentiment on a specific prompt without reflecting broader customer opinion.

For [ecommerce teams](/aeo-for/ecommerce)—especially considering how [AI-referred retail traffic converts](/blog/ai-referral-traffic-conversion)—measuring SKU-level placement and merchant selection is far more actionable than a general brand visibility score.

sections.heading: What AI Site Audits Check and Where They Fall Short
paragraphs: Traditional SEO site crawlers look for broken links, canonical tags, and Core Web Vitals. An AI site audit (often labeled a GEO audit or AI readiness scan) inspects a site from the perspective of language model retrieval bots and grounding agents. Because [most AI crawlers fetch raw HTML and skip JavaScript](/blog/do-ai-crawlers-render-javascript), content rendered client-side—such as pricing tables, product specs, or comparison matrices—can be invisible when an assistant tries to verify facts on your domain.

Across the 67 tools in this category, audits generally examine three areas: crawler access (checking [robots.txt rules for AI bots](/blog/robots-txt-ai-crawlers) like GPTBot, ClaudeBot, and PerplexityBot), machine readability (stripped HTML views, [structured data and llms.txt files](/blog/structured-data-for-ai-search)), and entity or passage clarity. Some platforms stop at a diagnostic scorecard, while others—such as Prominara, Indexly, and Canonry—generate the schema markup or configuration files directly.

The main limitation of any on-page AI audit is that [an engine-free content score cannot predict whether AI will cite you](/blog/can-content-scores-predict-ai-citations). Fixing technical blockers ensures [AI agents can read your website](/blog/can-ai-agents-read-your-website), which is necessary when a buyer asks an assistant about your product directly. However, earning citations on broad category prompts depends heavily on third-party corroboration, [citation analytics](/ai-visibility-tools/features/citation-analytics), and off-site authority that an on-page scanner cannot measure.

sections.heading: What Separates a Useful Audit From a Generic Checklist
paragraphs: Many tools repackage standard SEO linters as AI readiness scores. When evaluating an AI site audit, check whether the tool tests how AI retrieval systems actually interact with your pages or merely grades keyword density.

items.title: Raw HTML Inspection vs. Surface Grading

items.title: Transparent Checkpoints and Caveats

Stronger implementations specify their scope—such as Rankscale's 94 technical checkpoints, OtterlyAI's 25+ on-page GEO factors, or Passionfruit's 100+ URL signals—and state plainly, as Prominara does, that audit scores are diagnostics rather than placement guarantees.

items.title: Crawler Log Verification
items.body: Checking robots.txt tells you whether bots are allowed; server logs tell you whether they actually visit and where they get stuck. Tools that pair site audits with [AI crawler analytics](/ai-visibility-tools/features/ai-crawler-analytics)—such as Siteline, Scrunch, Canonry, and Cairrot—confirm whether your fixes result in real bot crawls.

items.title: Validation Against Live Prompts

Look for workflows that connect on-page fixes to [action recommendations](/ai-visibility-tools/features/action-recommendations) and re-run tracked prompts to measure whether citation rates or brand accuracy changed.

sections.heading: How AI Visibility Scores Work and Where They Fall Short
paragraphs: In [AI visibility tracking](/features/ai-visibility-tracking), a visibility score rolls up hundreds or thousands of individual prompt runs into a single percentage or index. At its simplest, the metric is the share of tracked runs in which an answer engine names your brand, aliases, or domain. Some platforms keep the math plain—Elmo defines visibility directly as the share of runs that mention your brand, alongside a separate [share of voice](/features/share-of-voice) metric comparing your mention rate against competitors. Other tools blend mention frequency with average ranking position, citation counts, or estimated prompt volume to produce a composite index.

The main limitation of any aggregate score is that [two tools will give the same brand very different numbers](/blog/why-ai-visibility-scores-differ) in the same week. A score is entirely downstream of the prompt set you choose, the engines you query, and how those prompts are weighted. If a tool samples raw model APIs without web search enabled, or weights top-of-funnel definitions the same as bottom-of-funnel vendor comparisons, the headline score can move while actual buyer discovery stays flat.

Because generative answers are non-deterministic, single-run snapshots are noisy. Reliable scoring requires [running prompts on a recurring schedule](/blog/ai-prompt-tracking) across real consumer interfaces and storing the underlying text so teams can verify why a score changed.

sections.heading: What to Check When Evaluating Visibility Scoring

items.title: Transparent Formula vs. Black-Box Index

In open-source Elmo, the mention detection, scoring, and aggregation code is inspectable in the repository, and every metric links back to the raw PostgreSQL answer text.

items.title: Real Consumer UI vs. Raw API Calls

items.title: Mention Detection and Alias Handling

Also check whether the tool separates [citation analytics](/ai-visibility-tools/features/citation-analytics) from text mentions, since AI engines frequently cite a domain without naming the brand in prose.

items.title: Sliceability by Engine, Tag, and Competitor
items.body: A single blended score hides engine-level swings. Look for tools that break visibility down per model, per prompt tag, and against [competitor benchmarks](/ai-visibility-tools/features/competitor-benchmarking) so you can tell whether a drop happened in ChatGPT, Perplexity, or Google AI Overviews.

sections.heading: How White-Label AI Visibility Platforms Work (and Where They Fall Short)
paragraphs: In the AI visibility category, vendors use the term "white-label" to describe three very different deliverables. At the most basic level, a tool lets you upload your agency logo to a PDF export or generate an unbranded link for [client reporting](/blog/ai-visibility-client-reporting). A step up from that is data-pipeline white-labeling: platforms expose [BI connectors](/ai-visibility-tools/features/bi-connectors) (such as Looker Studio or Databox) or a [REST API](/ai-visibility-tools/features/data-export-api) so your team can blend AI mention metrics into the client reporting portals you already maintain. At the top end, full multi-tenant platforms provide isolated client workspaces where clients log in under your agency's domain and branding.

The main operational limit for agencies is cost scaling. Unlike traditional rank trackers that check static SERPs, AI visibility tools must query multiple LLMs or scrape live consumer interfaces repeatedly to build a reliable sample. When vendors charge per prompt, per engine, or per brand workspace, an agency onboarding twenty clients can watch its software bill outpace its retainer margins.

To avoid per-seat and per-workspace markups, technical agencies often look to open-source software. Elmo is open-source (MIT) [AI visibility software for agencies](/aeo-for/agencies) that you can self-host for free or run on Elmo Cloud starting at $29/mo, with white-label options available. Because you can bring your own scraping provider and model API keys, your tracking costs scale at raw infrastructure rates, and you can share [AI visibility reports](/features/ai-visibility-reporting) with stakeholders who do not have an account.

sections.heading: What to Check When Evaluating Agency GEO Tools
paragraphs: Before committing your agency to an annual contract, test how the platform handles multi-client operations and data verification. A branded header on a chart will not save a client review if you cannot explain why a visibility score dropped.

items.title: Workspace Isolation and Access Controls
items.body: Check whether each client brand gets a truly separate workspace with its own prompt sets, [competitor benchmarks](/ai-visibility-tools/features/competitor-benchmarking), and user permissions. For example, GrackerAI includes multi-brand workspaces with SSO, SiteSignal allows unlimited team and client invitations at no extra cost, and WorkDuo reserves its white-labeled client portal for its enterprise tier.

items.title: Pre-Pitch Audit Workflows
items.body: Agencies need a fast way to audit prospects before a sales pitch without burning their main client prompt quota. Tools with built-in site audits or free report generators — such as OtterlyAI's 25-factor GEO Audit, PromptRush's free region-selectable visibility report, or GoVISIBLE's free audit — help teams scope new retainers.

items.title: Real UI Capture vs. API Calls
items.body: Clients check what you report by typing prompts into ChatGPT or Google themselves. Because API responses often differ from consumer interfaces, check whether the tool captures [real UI answers](/ai-visibility-tools/features/real-ui-answers) — a capability supported by tools like Elmo, Qwairy, Rankscale, Superlines, and Omnia.

items.title: BI Connectors and Raw Data Access
items.body: If your agency already standardizes client reporting in Looker Studio or custom dashboards, standalone PDF exports create extra manual work. Look for native Looker Studio connectors (offered by OtterlyAI, Local Falcon, LLM Pulse, SiteSignal, and Cairrot) or full [API and MCP access](/features/api-and-mcp) to pipe raw citation and sentiment data into your own system.

sections.heading: Choosing the Right Platform for Your Agency Model
paragraphs: The right tool depends on whether you sell AI visibility as an add-on to existing SEO retainers, as a standalone technical audit, or as a turnkey content execution service. If your clients ask why organic traffic is shifting and want unified search reporting, traditional SEO suites that have added AI tracking — such as SE Visible ($99/mo), Nightwatch (€79/mo), or the Semrush AI Toolkit ($99/mo) — let you keep keyword ranks and AI Overviews in one familiar workflow. Agencies focused on local businesses will find a closer fit in Local Falcon ($24.99/mo) or hyper-local trackers like Rank Prompt ($39/mo).

For agencies building dedicated AEO and GEO practices, standalone trackers offer broader model coverage and deeper [citation analytics](/ai-visibility-tools/features/citation-analytics). Rankscale ($20/mo) and Finseo (€84/mo) cover 10 to 17+ engines with [query fan-out](/ai-visibility-tools/features/query-fan-out) data, while Qwairy (€79/mo) provides EU data hosting and explicitly labels UI versus API results. If your agency sells done-for-you execution rather than monitoring alone, platforms like Frase ($39/mo), Sight AI ($99/mo), and Orchly.ai ($49/mo) bundle tracking with automated content workflows.

Finally, if your agency wants full control over its margins, branding, and methodology, consider open-source platforms like Elmo or Canonry. (Note that while GetCito also appears in the open-source category, [GetCito is a fork of Elmo's codebase](/blog/getcito-vs-elmo) that has shipped fewer updates since forking, so agencies evaluating it should use Elmo directly.) Self-hosting Elmo gives your agency an auditable PostgreSQL database of every raw prompt run, cited URL, and sentiment passage, with zero vendor lock-in.

faqs.question: What is the difference between white-label reports and a white-label client portal?
faqs.answer: White-label reports are static exports (like PDFs or CSVs) or unbranded share links that let you present visibility scores and citation data with your agency logo. A white-label client portal is a live, multi-tenant web dashboard hosted on your custom domain where clients log in to view their own brand workspaces.
